items.followUp: Describe single, double and triple covalent bonds, giving one example of each.

rubric.why: Identifies the sharing of electrons as the basis of a covalent bond.
rubric.description: Covalent bonds form when atoms share electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that atoms share electrons to form a covalent bond.

rubric.why: Identifies the number of shared electron pairs and gives a single-bond example.
rubric.description: A single covalent bond involves one shared pair of electrons; H2 is an example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both the one-pair description and a correct example.

rubric.why: Identifies the number of shared electron pairs and gives a double-bond example.
rubric.description: A double covalent bond involves two shared pairs of electrons; O2 is an example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both the two-pair description and a correct example.

rubric.why: Identifies the number of shared electron pairs and gives a triple-bond example.
rubric.description: A triple covalent bond involves three shared pairs of electrons; N2 is an example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both the three-pair description and a correct example.

modelAnswer: A covalent bond is formed when atoms share electrons.
A single covalent bond is formed by sharing one pair of electrons; for example, H2.
A double covalent bond is formed by sharing two pairs of electrons; for example, O2.
A triple covalent bond is formed by sharing three pairs of electrons; for example, N2.

items.followUp: Describe how to prepare a dilute solution from a concentrated solution, including the dilution formula.

rubric.why: States the relationship used to calculate the required volume for dilution.
rubric.description: Use the dilution formula M1V1 = M2V2.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct dilution formula.

rubric.why: Shows that the required amount of concentrated solution is determined before dilution.
rubric.description: Calculate the volume of concentrated solution required.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the required concentrated-solution volume is calculated.

rubric.why: Describes accurate measurement and transfer of the concentrated solution.
rubric.description: Measure the calculated volume with a pipette and transfer it to a volumetric flask containing some distilled water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for measuring and transferring the concentrated solution into the flask.

rubric.why: Completes the solution to the required volume and ensures it is uniform.
rubric.description: Add distilled water to the calibration mark, stopper the flask and mix thoroughly.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for making up to the mark and mixing; award 1 mark if only one of these steps is stated.

modelAnswer: Use the dilution formula M1V1 = M2V2 to calculate the volume of concentrated solution required.
Put some distilled water into a volumetric flask.
Measure the calculated volume of concentrated solution with a pipette and transfer it to the flask.
Add distilled water until the bottom of the meniscus reaches the calibration mark.
Stopper the flask and mix the solution thoroughly.
When diluting an acid, add the acid slowly to water, never water to acid.

rubric.why: Defines gram molecular mass as the mass of a mole of molecules expressed in grams.
rubric.description: Gram molecular mass is the mass in grams of one mole of a substance’s molecules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining it as the mass in grams of one mole of molecules.

rubric.why: States the numerical relationship to molecular mass.
rubric.description: Its numerical value is equal to the molecular mass of the substance.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that its numerical value equals the molecular mass.

modelAnswer: Gram molecular mass is the mass, in grams, of one mole of a substance’s molecules.
Its numerical value is equal to the molecular mass of the substance.

items.followUp: Name two radioisotopes used in medicine and state one use of each.

rubric.why: Names one radioisotope used to treat cancer.
rubric.description: Cobalt-60 is used in cancer treatment.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming cobalt-60 or another valid radioisotope used to treat cancer.

rubric.why: Names another radioisotope used to treat cancer.
rubric.description: Radium-226 is another radioisotope used in cancer treatment.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming a second valid radioisotope used to treat cancer.

modelAnswer: Cobalt-60 is used in the treatment of cancer.
Radium-226 is another radioisotope used in the treatment of cancer.

items.followUp: State the modern periodic law and identify the quantity on which it is based.

rubric.why: States that elemental properties show a periodic pattern.
rubric.description: The properties of elements are periodic.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the properties of elements are periodic.

rubric.why: Identifies atomic number as the basis of the periodic relationship.
rubric.description: The properties are periodic functions of atomic numbers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for specifying atomic number as the basis of the periodic law.

modelAnswer: The properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers.

items.followUp: Explain why atomic size generally increases down a group.

rubric.why: States the direction of the electronegativity trend down a group.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that electronegativity decreases down a group.

rubric.why: Explains the weaker attraction for shared electrons down a group.
rubric.description: The number of electron shells and shielding increase, so shared electrons are farther from the nucleus and experience less nuclear attraction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for connecting increased shells, shielding, or distance with weaker attraction for shared electrons.

modelAnswer: The number of electron shells and shielding increase, so the shared electrons are farther from the nucleus and experience less nuclear attraction.
